criterion_scores.reasoning: The text-generation workflow is mostly coherent, and the skill includes strong provenance, character-budget, personalization, and Notion-output rules. However, a load-bearing required path is wrong: Step 3b.5 instructs use of removed Gamma MCP (`mcp__claude_ai_Gamma__generate`, line 285), and Step 7 still says the carousel auto-renders via Canva MCP (line 508). Because every LinkedIn post is required to ship with a visual brief/render path, this is not a cosmetic issue. Additional correctness slips include the wrong execution order at line 282 and the no-people error handler incorrectly skipping Step 5 post optimization at line 607.

The skill covers the major required deliverables: Upcoming Week post, per-event post, visual brief, connection notes, autoresearch, prepared questions, Notion writes, summary, and error handling. The deterministic missing-reference check reports no missing `.claude/` references. Completeness is still weakened by the wrong prepared-questions write pointer at line 575 and by mandatory visual execution depending on removed tooling; the parts are present, but one important output path is not reliably executable as written.

Frontmatter and project-skill naming are correct: `name: pre-event-content` has no `alex:` prefix, and the file is in the expected `.claude/skills/` area. The artifact generally respects reference-file hierarchy and Notion Content Draft conventions. The main convention/source-of-truth defect is stale visual-tool routing: Step 7 embeds Canva MCP as the auto-render path (line 508) while Step 3b.5 makes Gamma the default, and both conflict with the tombstone check. This violates current tool/source-of-truth discipline.

The skill otherwise avoids many content anti-patterns by enforcing provenance exclusions, Learn-More Sets, character counts, personalization gates, and anti-pattern scans. But it substantially resurrects tombstoned visual-generation tooling: Gamma is made the default generator for all visual content at line 277, and the workflow calls a removed Gamma MCP at line 285; Step 7 also preserves the old Canva MCP generator instruction at line 508. That is a major anti-pattern under the rubric and the supplied tombstone check.

The artifact has many useful diagnostics and quality gates: explicit failure handling, character counts, source checks, quality gates, score thresholds, and summary counts. However, stale and contradictory workflow labels make failures harder to understand: line 282 says Step 4 writes the Content Draft even though writes are Step 7; line 471 says Step 4 produces one best connection note despite Step 4 requiring two variants when possible; and line 607 mislabels Step 5 as DM generation. These inconsistencies would confuse execution and debugging, though the skill is not opaque overall.
